pre_inference_amendment.reason: Pre-inference fairness audit discovered that STRIPED geometry under v1.0 had a duty-cycle clamping bug (min(dose * 2, 1.0) * stripe_h) that truncated all striped masks at 50% occlusion, giving 0 observations above 50% occlusion across all images. This prevented fair common-support comparison in the upper dose regime (0.50-0.70).
pre_inference_amendment.evidence_used: results/phase25_occlusion_topology/pre_inference_fairness_summary.json (geometry feasibility audit only; ZERO model inference inspected).
changes: 1. STRIPED geometry redesigned to pixel-exact adaptive stripe allocation: k_total = round(dose * H) rows occluded, partitioned across min(5, max(1, H // 4)) stripe periods. Verified: mean dose error drops from 0.0586 to 0.0081, max error drops from 0.3667 to 0.0333.

2. Confirmatory common-support range established across all 4 topologies from achieved dose 0.00 to 0.75 partitioned into 8 balanced bins: [0.00, 0.05), [0.05, 0.15), [0.15, 0.25), [0.25, 0.35), [0.35, 0.45), [0.45, 0.55), [0.55, 0.65), [0.65, 0.75). Each bin contains between 89 and 215 observations per topology.
3. Confirmatory topology comparisons and ED50 estimation use binned achieved-dose common support.
4. Protocol v1.0 is preserved permanently without modification.

part_01_hypotheses.H0: Phase 23 frame-success rate does not vary across occlusion topologies (CENTER, OUTER_RING, STRIPED, RANDOM_PATCH) at matched achieved dose levels
part_01_hypotheses.H1_primary: Frame success rate at IoU >= 0.50 declines monotonically with increasing achieved dose for all topologies
part_01_hypotheses.H2_topology: The dose-response curve shape differs between topologies — specifically, the dose at which frame success drops below 50% (ED50) differs by topology
part_01_hypotheses.H3_scale_interaction: The dose-response relationship is moderated by target object scale (target_area_quartile), with smaller objects showing steeper decline
part_01_hypotheses.note: All hypotheses are neutral with respect to direction. We do not predict which topology causes faster degradation.

part_02_dose_grid.dose_unit: fraction of annotation-box area occluded (achieved, not requested)

feasibility_result.common_support_status: EXCELLENT — all 4 topologies span achieved doses 0.00 to 0.75 with substantial sample size in all 8 analysis bins.

definitions.CENTER: Centered rectangle inside annotation box. Mask aspect ratio matches box aspect ratio. Mask area = dose * box_area, so side scale = sqrt(dose).
definitions.OUTER_RING: Full annotation box filled, then a centered rectangular hole cut out. Hole area = (1 - dose) * box_area, so hole scale = sqrt(1 - dose).
definitions.STRIPED: Pixel-exact adaptive horizontal stripes within annotation box. k_total = round(dose * box_height) rows occluded, distributed evenly across min(5, max(1, box_height // 4)) stripe periods.
definitions.RANDOM_PATCH: Random rectangular patches placed within annotation box until target dose fraction is approximately achieved. Patch positions and sizes are deterministic via seeded PRNG.

part_03_mask_geometries.occluder_fill_description: Neutral gray (128, 128, 128) — fixed across all topologies

part_04_occlusion_measurements.achieved_dose_definition: mask_pixels_in_box / box_pixels, where mask_pixels_in_box counts the number of mask-covered pixels strictly within the YOLO annotation bounding box

part_05_geometry_feasibility.method: Computed achieved dose for all 86 frames × 4 topologies × 15 doses in dry-run mode (no images written). Dose error = |achieved_dose - requested_dose|.
findings: CENTER and OUTER_RING achieve tight dose control across all doses
STRIPED achieves pixel-exact dose control (mean error = 0.0081, max error = 0.0333) with full range [0.00, 0.72]
RANDOM_PATCH achieves reasonable dose control (mean error = 0.0242) with stochastic variance
All 4 topologies provide continuous, overlapping common support from 0.00 to 0.75
part_05_geometry_feasibility.mitigation: All analyses use achieved_dose as the independent variable. Confirmatory comparisons use the 8 pre-declared common support bins.

part_06_fairness_balance_audit.balance_note: Each source frame is tested under all 4 topologies × 15 doses = 60 views. This ensures within-frame comparison across topologies. The 66:20 land_pad:land_pad2 ratio reflects the protected test split and is not rebalanced.

part_07_source_population.source_images: kios_real_stress/clean/images/test/ — original clean images ONLY (no pre-degraded images)
part_07_source_population.labels_unchanged: YOLO labels are copied unchanged from clean condition. Occlusion does not change ground-truth annotation.

part_09_primary_outcome.name: frame_success
part_09_primary_outcome.matching_rule: one-to-one confidence-ranked greedy matching against ground-truth boxes
part_09_primary_outcome.confidence_handling: All predictions above conf=0.001 are included. No secondary confidence threshold.

part_10_secondary_outcomes.name: best_iou
part_10_secondary_outcomes.definition: Maximum IoU between any predicted box and the ground-truth target

part_10_secondary_outcomes.name: best_confidence
part_10_secondary_outcomes.definition: Confidence score of the highest-confidence prediction

part_10_secondary_outcomes.name: tp
part_10_secondary_outcomes.definition: Number of true positive detections (predictions matched to ground truth at IoU >= 0.50)

part_10_secondary_outcomes.name: pred_count
part_10_secondary_outcomes.definition: Total number of predictions above conf=0.001

part_11_statistical_design.repeated_measures: Each source frame observed under 4 topologies × 15 dose levels = 60 views
part_11_statistical_design.clustering: Clustered bootstrap resampling at the source-frame level (not the view level)
part_11_statistical_design.dose_response_model: Non-parametric: frame_success_rate computed at each achieved_dose bin, per topology
part_11_statistical_design.comparison_method: Within-frame paired comparison: for each frame, compare frame_success at matched achieved_dose bins across topologies

tests: Dose-response slope: is frame_success_rate monotonically decreasing with dose?
Topology comparison: does ED50 differ between topologies?
Scale interaction: does target_area_quartile moderate dose-response?

hierarchy.correction: None — explicitly labeled as exploratory, not used for confirmatory conclusions

part_13_threshold_criterion.ed50_definition: The lowest achieved_dose at which frame_success_rate drops below 0.50 for a given topology, estimated by linear interpolation between adjacent dose bins
part_13_threshold_criterion.change_point_method: Binary segmented regression on frame_success ~ achieved_dose, choosing the breakpoint that minimizes total RSS
part_13_threshold_criterion.note: These criteria are locked before any Phase 23 inference on topology-occluded images

A.description: All topologies produce indistinguishable dose-response curves
A.interpretation: Occlusion topology does not matter — only total occluded area drives detection failure. The Phase 23 detector responds to area loss, not spatial pattern.

B.description: CENTER causes faster degradation than OUTER_RING
B.interpretation: Central features (center of landing pad) are more critical for Phase 23 detection than peripheral features. This is consistent with attention-based feature extraction.

C.description: OUTER_RING causes faster degradation than CENTER
C.interpretation: Edge features (concentric ring boundaries) are more critical for Phase 23 detection. This would support an edge-dependent detection mechanism.

D.description: STRIPED causes faster degradation than geometric topologies
D.interpretation: Feature disruption by alternating visible/occluded regions is more damaging than contiguous occlusion at the same dose. This suggests the detector relies on spatial continuity.

E.interpretation: Smaller objects are more sensitive to occlusion because they have fewer pixels carrying discriminative features. This is expected and documented as a known limitation of small-object detection.

part_15_topology_generator.determinism: All randomness is seeded from SHA-256 of (GLOBAL_SEED=20261001, frame_name, topology, dose). Same inputs always produce byte-identical outputs.
part_15_topology_generator.atomic_writes: Images are written via tempfile + fsync + os.replace for crash safety
part_15_topology_generator.decode_validation: Source images are opened and converted to RGB before mask application
part_15_topology_generator.sha_verification: Source image SHA-256 and output image SHA-256 are recorded per view

part_18_power_study_size.note: N=86 is the protected population size. This is NOT inflated by the 60× repeated measures per frame. Statistical inference is clustered at the source-frame level.
part_18_power_study_size.generalization_scope: Results apply only to these 86 frames under synthetic occlusion with neutral-gray fill. No generalization to other datasets, targets, or occluder materials.

part_19_protocol_freeze.no_modifications_after_freeze: Any modification after Phase 23 inference begins constitutes a protocol violation and must be documented as a deviation

dry_run.description: Generates masks, computes achieved doses, writes CSV with empty prediction columns. Does NOT run model inference. Does NOT write images.

execute.description: Generates images, runs Phase 23 inference, fills prediction columns, computes frame_success.
